rule: An urban area has a garrison when one of its municipalities has an installation of tier “major” or “base”, or one of its hexes lies in a training ground.

rules.installations: OpenStreetMap military areas (landuse=military and military=base, barracks, airfield, naval_base, range, office and, inside military land, training_area and danger_area), each on the hex where its centre falls. An area inside a larger one counts as part of it, and one without a name takes that of its largest named part. Guardia Civil and police posts, civilian sites (Navantia, AENA), former and heritage sites (old barracks, bunkers, museums) and areas without a name are left out.
rules.branch: The branch comes from the OpenStreetMap operator; failing that, from the name («Base Aérea», «Arsenal», «Acuartelamiento», «Campo de Maniobras y Tiro»…); failing that, from the tag (airfield or naval base), and failing that, from the operator Wikidata gives the item within 1.5 km. The rest is left as “other”.
rules.tier: No headcount is published for each base, so size comes from the ground inside its boundary: “major” from 10 km², “base” from 0.5 km² and “site” for the rest, including those that are only a point.
rules.ranges: The 15 largest OpenStreetMap military boundaries of at least 20 km² (manoeuvre and firing grounds, firing ranges and the largest bases). They take the hexes whose centre falls inside; one that covers no centre is drawn on the hex of its point. A hex is about 87 km², so small grounds look larger than they are.
rules.garrisons: An urban area has a garrison when one of its municipalities has an installation of tier “major” or “base”, or one of its hexes lies in a training ground.
rules.joint: Rota and Morón are used jointly with the United States under the 1988 Agreement on Defense Cooperation (Convenio de Cooperación para la Defensa, BOE of 6 May 1989, amended in 2002, 2012 and 2015); they remain Spanish bases.

caveats: The Ministry of Defence publishes no open list of its installations or their boundaries: the ones on this map are OpenStreetMap's, drawn by volunteers, and some cover only part of a site (the San Gregorio training ground, for example). Nor does it publish each base's headcount, so they are measured by area, not by personnel. The branch is inferred from the operator or the name and can be wrong on a shared site.
